engine.name: GUITinstal Universal Engine
engine.promise: Paste a repository. Analyze it. Install it. Launch it.
notes: The catalog is data. The engine modules read it; they never hardcode a second copy of it.
installMode says how a runtime can reach a machine. status says whether GUITinstal can do it today.
A runtime is never installed from an untrusted mirror and never without a published checksum.

runtimes.label: Git
runtimes.summary: The version control every clone depends on.

versions.policy: pinned release of Git for Windows, updated with a new digest and a fresh clone proof

checksum.where: Git for Windows publishes no checksum file for MinGit; GUITinstal pins the digest of the exact supported asset and records it in its install manifest

signature.where: the Git for Windows binaries are signed by Johannes Schindelin (checked after unpacking)

runtimes.verification: run git --version, confirm git-remote-https is present, and clone a repository with the managed copy
runtimes.uninstall: delete <userData>/tools/git; nothing outside the tools folder is touched

runtimes.label: GitHub CLI
runtimes.summary: Optional helper for repositories that need the gh command line.

versions.policy: latest stable published by the vendor

checksum.where: the release assets, next to the archive

runtimes.verification: run the version command; a non-zero exit means the install failed
runtimes.uninstall: delete the destination folder; nothing outside <userData>/tools is touched
runtimes.reason: Resolver returns 200 OK with SHA-256 verification; optional helper for repositories needing gh command

runtimes.label: GCC
runtimes.summary: The C and C++ compiler used by many native projects on Windows.

runtimes.uninstall: delete the destination folder; nothing outside <userData>/tools is touched
runtimes.reason: There is no official standalone GCC build for Windows. It only exists through a third-party toolchain, so GUITstal points at MSYS2 instead of shipping a build of unknown origin.
